full_text_en:
Gansu Qianjinda Mining Development Group Co., Ltd. v. Wancheng Business Dongshengmiao Co., Ltd. — dispute over profit distribution

[2024] SPC Min Zai No. 23

[Ruling Summary]

The necessary condition for a shareholder to demand the company distribute profits is the submission of a shareholders' resolution containing a specific distribution plan. A specific profit distribution plan shall include specific distribution details such as the amount of profits to be distributed, the distribution policy, the scope of distribution, and the time of distribution. The key to determining whether a profit distribution plan is specific lies in whether the specific amount of profits that the claimant seeking distribution is entitled to under the plan can be determined based on the available information. If the shareholders' resolution of the company determines the total amount of profits to be distributed and the time of distribution, and in conjunction with the distribution policy stipulated in the company's articles of association that shareholders receive dividends according to their capital contribution ratios, the specific amount of profits that a shareholder is entitled to under the plan can be determined, then the profit distribution plan contained in the shareholders' resolution shall be considered specific.

Once a shareholders' resolution containing a specific distribution plan is made, the abstract right to claim profit distribution is converted into a specific right to claim profit distribution, transforming from a shareholder's membership right into a ordinary creditor's right independent of shareholder rights. When a shareholder transfers their equity, the abstract right to claim profit distribution is transferred accordingly, while the specific right to claim profit distribution is not transferred with the equity transfer unless expressly agreed in the contract. When the time for distribution of profits arrives and the company fails to distribute, the right holder may directly request the company to pay the profits in accordance with the specific distribution plan contained in the resolution.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2021) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 23

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Gansu Qianjinda Mining Development Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 1604C, Block 1, Zhonghai International Office Building, No. 298 Jingning Road, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Li Wei, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Yin Handong, lawyer of Beijing Shengfa Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Luo Ruifang, lawyer of Tianjin Yungong (Beijing) Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Wancheng Business Dongshengmiao Co., Ltd., domiciled at Bayin Town, Wuhouqi, Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Ye Guojun, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Ding Canping, lawyer of Beijing Zhouzhi Tong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Quan Yinghong, lawyer of Gansu Deyansheng Law Firm.

In the dispute over profit distribution between the applicant for retrial, Gansu Qianjinda Mining Development Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qianjinda Company), and the respondent, Wancheng Business Dongshengmiao Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wancheng Company), the applicant appealed against the Civil Judgment (2019) Nei Min Zhong No. 349 of the High People's Court of Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region to this Court for retrial. On April 14, 2020, this Court issued the Civil Ruling (2020) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 419, granting the retrial. This Court formed a collegiate panel according to law and held a hearing in the case. The applicant for retrial, Qianjinda Company, and the respondent, Wancheng Company, appeared before the court. The case is now concluded.

Qianjinda Company applied for retrial, requesting: 1. To set aside the Civil Judgment (2019) Nei Min Zhong No. 349 of the High People's Court of Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, and to uphold Item 1 of the Civil Judgment (2018) Nei 08 Min Chu No. 60 of the Intermediate People's Court of Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, i.e., to order Wancheng Company to pay Qianjinda Company the unpaid profit for 2013 of RMB 29,888,366.29, plus interest calculated from September 12, 2018 at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period until the date of full payment. 2. To set aside Item 2 of the Civil Judgment (2018) Nei 08 Min Chu No. 60 of the Intermediate People's Court of Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, and to order Wancheng Company to pay Qianjinda Company the unpaid profit for 2014 of RMB 4,459,170.94, plus corresponding interest until the date of full discharge. Facts and reasons: 1. It is the legal right of Qianjinda Company to demand payment of the unpaid profit for 2013 already decided to be distributed by the shareholders' meeting in proportion to its shareholding. The capital contribution ratio of Qianjinda Company is consistent with its shareholding ratio. The shareholders of Wancheng Company did not agree not to distribute dividends according to capital contribution ratios. Pursuant to Article 34 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, Qianjinda Company is entitled to receive dividends in proportion to its shareholding. Regardless of whether the distribution ratio for the unpaid profit for 2013 in the Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 of 2014 is clear, it does not affect Qianjinda Company's right to receive the corresponding profits from the decided unpaid profit based on its 52.50% equity. 2. The second-instance judgment, holding that the unpaid profit for 2013 could not be paid according to the capital contribution ratio stipulated in the company's articles of association, has no legal basis and illegally deprives Qianjinda Company of its legal creditor's right. The articles of association of Wancheng Company stipulate "distributing dividends according to capital contribution ratios." When the shareholders' resolution does not specify the profit distribution ratio for each shareholder, applying the distribution ratio stipulated in the company's articles of association to pay dividends to shareholders is in line with the common intention of all shareholders and fully reflects the autonomy of the company's will. In Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 of 2014, the amount of remaining unpaid profit for 2013 was established, and the time of payment was specified. In conjunction with the distribution ratio stipulated in the articles of association, the distribution plan shall be deemed specific and clear. 3. It should be determined that the distribution plan for the unpaid profit for 2013 is specific and clear. The articles of association of Wancheng Company stipulate distributing dividends according to capital contribution ratios. The determination of whether the distribution plan for the unpaid profit for 2013 is specific and clear should not rely solely on Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 of 2014, but also on the company's articles of association. 4. According to the content of Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 of 2014 and the company's articles of association, the unpaid profit for 2013 is a ascertainable creditor's right, and Qianjinda Company is entitled to demand payment. 5. The second-instance judgment rejected Qianjinda Company's claim for payment of the unpaid profit for 2013, which effectively supports the company's non-compliance with its articles of association, is clearly illegal, and has a negative social impact. 6. Qianjinda Company's claim for payment of the unpaid profit for 2014 is legally well-founded and should be supported. The "Minutes of the Second Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting of Wancheng Business Dongshengmiao Co., Ltd. in 2014" (hereinafter referred to as the "Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting Minutes") dated June 25, 2014, bears the seals and signatures of attending shareholders and their representatives, and the meeting decided to distribute dividends quarterly in 2014. Although the audit report does not constitute the company's distribution plan, it can prove the distribution plan actually implemented by Wancheng Company and the amount of profits to be distributed for 2014. It should be determined that the amount of profits to be distributed for 2014 is specific and clear. 7. Certain facts were not fully investigated in the original trial. On September 24, 2015, Qianjinda Company transferred the registration of its 52.5% equity in Wancheng Company to its wholly-owned subsidiary Gansu Qianjinda Asset Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qianjinda Asset Management Company). On June 8, 2015, Qianjinda Company and Zhao Jintang entered into an "Equity Transfer Agreement," agreeing to transfer all equity of Qianjinda Asset Management Company to Zhao Jintang for RMB 480 million. However, on December 11, 2015, Qianjinda Company and Zhao Jintang signed another "Equity Transfer Agreement" stipulating that the equity transfer price would be agreed upon in a supplementary agreement. Zhao Jintang actually paid RMB 400 million in equity consideration, but the parties have not yet agreed on the amount of the equity transfer price. The original judgment found unclear facts.

Wancheng Company argued in defense: 1. The provisions regarding the distribution amount and method in Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 of 2014 and the Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting Minutes are not sufficiently accurate, specific, or operable, and do not constitute a distribution plan as referred to in judicial interpretations. Although in June 2016, there was over RMB 42 million in Wancheng Company's financial account, RMB 40 million of that was due to the Bank of China for a matured loan, rendering it impossible to distribute dividends. Furthermore, the Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting Minutes are not a regular shareholders' resolution and do not constitute a specific distribution plan. 2. When Qianjinda Company transferred its equity, there were no liabilities or unpaid amounts recorded in Wancheng Company's accounts, and there were no relevant records or disclosures, indicating that there were no undistributed profits at that time. 3. Qianjinda Company did not file the lawsuit until September 2018, which was triggered by its loss in another case in July of that year. Filing the lawsuit four years later is unreasonable and exceeds the statute of limitations; it should be deemed that Qianjinda Company knew or should have known that no specific distribution plan existed.

Qianjinda Company filed a lawsuit at the court of first instance with the following claims: 1. Order Wancheng Company to pay Qianjinda Company the unpaid profit for 2013 of RMB 29,888,366.29; 2. Order Wancheng Company to pay Qianjinda Company the unpaid profit for 2014 of RMB 4,459,170.94; 3. Order Wancheng Company to bear the losses caused to Qianjinda Company due to overdue payment (based on RMB 34,347,537.23, calculated at an annual interest rate of 6% from December 22, 2015 to the date of actual payment); 4. The litigation costs shall be borne by Wancheng Company.

The court of first instance found the following facts: On July 30, 2013, Qianjinda Company changed its original name from Hainan Qianjinda Mining Group Co., Ltd. to the current name Gansu Qianjinda Mining Development Group Co., Ltd., holding 52.5% of the shares of Wancheng Company. On February 19, 2014, Linhe Dezhang United Certified Public Accountants Firm (hereinafter referred to as Dezhang Accounting Firm) conducted the 2013 financial audit of Wancheng Company and issued the Audit Report (Lin De Hui Shen Zi [2014] No. 019). The profit and profit distribution statement in the audit report showed that the net profit of Wancheng Company for 2013 was RMB 169,649,601.28, the distributable profits for shareholders were RMB 218,930,221.51, the dividends already paid were RMB 162,000,000, and the undistributed profits were RMB 56,930,221.51. On March 27, 2014, the shareholders of Wancheng Company, namely Zijin Mining Group Co., Ltd., Bayannur Zijin Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd., and Qianjinda Company, held a shareholders' meeting and adopted Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 (Wan Cheng Gu Zi [2014] No. 2), resolving: The total profit realized by the company for 2013 was RMB 227,050,779.10, the distributable profits for shareholders were RMB 218,930,221.51, the dividends already paid for the year were RMB 162,000,000, and the remaining undistributed profits of RMB 56,930,221.51 were temporarily unpaid, to be fully distributed before June 2014. On June 25, 2014, Zijin Mining Group Co., Ltd. and Qianjinda Company held the second extraordinary shareholders' meeting in 2014 and formed the Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting Minutes, Article 6 of which stated: The meeting agreed to distribute the undistributed profits for 2013 before the end of July, and to distribute dividends quarterly in 2014. On January 28, 2015, Dezhang Accounting Firm conducted the 2014 financial audit of Wancheng Company and issued the Audit Report (Lin De Hui Shen Zi [2015] No. 004). The profit and profit distribution statement in the audit report showed that the net profit for 2014 was RMB 53,583,822.26, the undistributed profits for 2013 were RMB 56,930,221.51, the distributable profits for shareholders were RMB 105,423,880.44, the dividends payable were RMB 40,000,000, and the undistributed profits were RMB 65,423,880.44. On September 24, 2015, Qianjinda Company transferred the registration of its 52.5% equity in Wancheng Company to its wholly-owned subsidiary Qianjinda Asset Management Company. On June 18, 2015, Qianjinda Company and Zhao Jintang signed an "Equity Transfer Agreement," whereby Qianjinda Company transferred 100% equity of its wholly-owned subsidiary Qianjinda Asset Management Company to Zhao Jintang for RMB 480 million. Article 6.3 of the agreement stipulated: "After the signing of this agreement, Party A undertakes not to directly or indirectly distribute dividends from Qianjinda Asset Management Company or Wancheng Company, not to use funds from the capital accounts of Qianjinda Asset Management Company or Wancheng Company, and not to engage in any act that may reduce the shareholder's equity of Party B." On December 17, 2015, the 100% equity of Qianjinda Asset Management Company was transferred from Qianjinda Company to the third party Zhao Jintang. On October 10, 2017, Qianjinda Company sent a "Company Letter" to Wancheng Company, Zijin Mining Group Co., Ltd., Bayannur Zijin Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd., Qianjinda Asset Management Company, and Zhao Jintang. The main content of the letter was: Qianjinda Company demanded Wancheng Company pay Qianjinda Company the profit of RMB 34,732,804.98 before June 18, 2015. Qianjinda Company sent the letter to Wancheng Company, its shareholders, and Zhao Jintang via SF Express, and the relevant personnel of each company signed for the letter.

Separately found: For fiscal year 2012, Wancheng Company implemented the Shareholders' Resolution No. 1 (Wan Cheng Gu Zi [2013] No. 1) and distributed profits to shareholders in cash according to their shareholding ratios.

The court of first instance held that profit distribution is a fundamental right of shareholders. On March 27, 2014, the shareholders of Wancheng Company, namely Zijin Mining Group Co., Ltd., Bayannur Zijin Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd., and Qianjinda Company, held a shareholders' meeting and adopted Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 (Wan Cheng Gu Zi [2014] No. 2), which was signed and sealed by all shareholders. The content of the resolution did not violate any relevant laws or administrative regulations and shall be deemed valid. The resolution decided to distribute the remaining undistributed profits for 2013 of RMB 56,930,221.51 before June 2014. On June 25, 2014, Zijin Mining Group Co., Ltd. and Qianjinda Company held the second extraordinary shareholders' meeting in 2014 and formed the Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting Minutes, which further clarified the agreement to distribute the undistributed profits for 2013 before the end of July and to distribute dividends quarterly in 2014. The shareholders' resolution and meeting minutes have specified the amount and time of distribution for the undistributed profits for 2013. Although Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 did not specify the specific amount or form of distribution for each shareholder, in fiscal year 2012, Wancheng Company also implemented Shareholders' Resolution No. 1 and distributed profits to shareholders in cash according to their shareholding ratios, a fact admitted by both parties. According to the distribution principle for 2012, the undistributed profits of Wancheng Company for 2013 were RMB 56,930,221.51. Calculated based on Qianjinda Company's shareholding ratio of 52.5%, the profit distributable to Qianjinda Company was RMB 29,888,366.29 (RMB 56,930,221.51 × 52.5%). Therefore, Wancheng Company's defense that the amount and form of dividends in Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 were unclear is untenable. On September 24, 2015, Qianjinda Company transferred the registration of its 52.5% equity in Wancheng Company to its wholly-owned subsidiary Qianjinda Asset Management Company. On June 18, 2015, Qianjinda Company transferred 100% equity of its wholly-owned subsidiary Qianjinda Asset Management Company to Zhao Jintang. Qianjinda Company and Zhao Jintang signed the "Equity Transfer Agreement," Article 6.3 of which provided: "After the signing of this agreement, Party A undertakes not to directly or indirectly distribute dividends from the management company or Wancheng Company, not to use funds from the capital accounts of the management company or Wancheng Company, and not to engage in any act that may reduce the shareholder's equity of Party B." The undistributed profits for 2013 and 2014 before June 18, 2015 were not explicitly transferred to Zhao Jintang, nor was it clear whether the transfer price in the agreement included the undistributed profits for 2013 and 2014. Before the company makes a profit distribution resolution, shareholders enjoy an abstract right to claim profit distribution, which is a shareholder right based on membership and a component of equity. When a shareholder transfers their membership, all rights, including the right to claim profit distribution, are transferred together. After the company makes a profit distribution resolution, shareholders enjoy a specific right to claim profit distribution. This right arises from the abstract right to claim profit distribution as a membership right but is independent of the profit distribution right and shareholder membership, and is essentially a ordinary creditor's right. When a shareholder transfers their membership, unless otherwise specified, the profits determined before the formation of the profit distribution resolution belong to the original shareholder, who may still claim the profits from the company based on the profit distribution resolution. Now, Wancheng Company argues that it does not owe Qianjinda Company undistributed dividends, but it has not provided evidence that it distributed the dividends payable for 2013 to Qianjinda Company. Therefore, it shall bear the consequences of failing to provide evidence. Qianjinda Company's claim for Wancheng Company to pay the unpaid profit for 2013 of RMB 29,888,366.29 (RMB 56,930,221.51 × 52.5%) is supported by the court. As for Qianjinda Company's claim for unpaid profit for 2014 of RMB 4,459,170.94, the Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting Minutes only mentioned quarterly distribution in 2014 but did not set forth a specific profit distribution plan for 2014. Moreover, the minutes do not constitute a valid shareholders' resolution. Therefore, the court does not support Qianjinda Company's claim.

Regarding whether this case has exceeded the statutory limitation period. The limitation period shall be calculated from the date when the right holder knows or should have known that his rights have been damaged and who the obligor is. On September 24, 2015, Qianjinda Company transferred its 52.5% equity in Wancheng Company to Qianjinda Asset Management Company, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Qianjinda Company; on December 17, 2015, 100% equity of Qianjinda Asset Management Company was transferred from Qianjinda Company to a third party, Zhao Jintang. Prior to this, Qianjinda Company had been the controlling shareholder and main business operator of Wancheng Company, holding a dual identity as both the right holder and the obligor, making it impossible for it to assert rights against itself. Therefore, the limitation period in this case should be calculated from December 17, 2015, when Qianjinda Company withdrew from Wancheng Company, i.e., when Qianjinda Company ceased to be the controlling shareholder of Wancheng Company. On October 10, 2017, Qianjinda Company mailed a "Company Letter" to Wancheng Company and its shareholders, Zijin Mining Group Co., Ltd., Bayannaoer Zijin Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd., Qianjinda Asset Management Company, and Zhao Jintang, requesting that Wancheng Company pay the profits due before June 18, 2015. This act should be deemed as an interruption of the limitation period. From that date to September 12, 2018, when Qianjinda Company filed the lawsuit, the statutory limitation period had not been exceeded. Therefore, the court does not support Wancheng Company's defense that this case has exceeded the limitation period.

Regarding Qianjinda Company's request that Wancheng Company bear losses for late payment calculated at an annual interest rate of 6% from December 22, 2015, to the date of actual payment. Since the shareholders' resolution did not include such an agreement, this claim lacks legal basis, and the court does not support it. However, interest shall be calculated from the date when Qianjinda Company asserted its rights, at the same type loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period, until the date of full payment.

In summary, the court supported Qianjinda Company's reasonable claims and rendered the civil judgment (2018) Nei 08 Min Chu No. 60 on February 19, 2019. Pursuant to Article 4 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 13(1), 14, and 15 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (IV) (hereinafter referred to as Judicial Interpretation IV of the Company Law), the judgment ordered: 1. Wancheng Company shall pay Qianjinda Company the profit distributable for the year 2013 in the amount of RMB 29,888,366.29 within fifteen days from the effective date of the judgment, and bear interest on such profit at the same type loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period from September 12, 2018, until the date of actual payment; 2. Qianjinda Company's other claims are dismissed. If Wancheng Company fails to perform the monetary payment obligation within the period specified in the judgment, it shall double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The case acceptance fee of RMB 213,537.68 shall be borne by Wancheng Company in the amount of RMB 185,815.14 and by Qianjinda Company in the amount of RMB 27,722.54; the preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Wancheng Company.

Qianjinda Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed with the following requests: 1. Uphold item 1 of the first-instance judgment; 2. Set aside item 2 of the first-instance judgment and order Wancheng Company to pay Qianjinda Company the unpaid profit for the year 2014 in the amount of RMB 4,459,170.94, with interest from September 12, 2018, at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period until the date of actual payment.

Wancheng Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed with the following requests: 1. Set aside the first-instance judgment; 2. Dismiss all of Qianjinda Company's claims; 3. Order Qianjinda Company to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances.

During the second instance, Qianjinda Company submitted the following new evidence: Evidence 1, the articles of association of Wancheng Company and amendments thereto, to prove that the articles of association of Wancheng Company explicitly provide that profits are distributed according to shareholding ratios. Evidence 2, the reconciliation statement, payment voucher, and receipt notice for the payment of RMB 21 million in profit for the year 2014 by Wancheng Company to Qianjinda Company, to prove that the "Minutes of the Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting" dated June 25, 2014, clearly stipulated quarterly profit distribution for 2014, and that Wancheng Company had already paid RMB 21 million in cash to Qianjinda Company. Wancheng Company argued in its cross-examination that, regarding Evidence 1, the authenticity could not be verified due to the lack of the original, and the purpose of proof was not accepted; according to Judicial Interpretation IV of the Company Law, determining profit distribution based on the articles of association is only a special case under the law, and the articles of association cannot determine the specific plan for profit distribution. The amendments to the articles of association are irrelevant to this case and do not contain any provisions on profit distribution. Regarding Evidence 2, the authenticity is recognized, but the purpose of proof is not accepted; the remarks all indicate that the payments are for goods, not profit distribution.

Wancheng Company submitted the following new evidence: Evidence 1, Mining Rights Appraisal Report No. 2015-024, to prove that the appraised value of the mining rights in 2015 was RMB 368,573,200, which included fixed asset investments, and the appraised value of machinery, equipment, and structures was RMB 63,081,200, so the total company value in 2015 was RMB 431,654,400. The equity price agreed between Qianjinda Company and Zhao Jintang was RMB 480 million, so the equity transfer price did not exclude profit distribution, which had already been accounted for in the transfer price. Evidence 2, Shareholders' Resolution No. 1 (2013), to prove that the shareholders' resolution of January 22, 2013, clearly stipulated the distribution ratio and the specific amount of profit each shareholder should receive for profit distribution, and also explicitly provided that the specific amount of profit distribution for 2013 would be determined after the year-end audit. Qianjinda Company argued in its cross-examination that, regarding Evidence 1, the appraisal report is irrelevant to this case; the equity transfer agreement signed between Qianjinda Company and Zhao Jintang on June 18, 2015, set the equity transfer price through negotiation between the parties, not based on the appraisal result. The authenticity of Evidence 2 is recognized, but the purpose of proof is not accepted. The court conducted a comprehensive evaluation of the above evidence.

The facts found in the second instance were consistent with those found in the first instance, and the court confirmed them.

The court of second instance held that this case is a dispute over company profit distribution. Article 14 of Judicial Interpretation IV of the Company Law provides: "If a shareholder submits a valid resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders that contains a specific distribution plan and requests the company to distribute profits, and the company refuses to distribute profits and its defense that the resolution cannot be implemented is not established, the people's court shall order the company to distribute profits to the shareholder in accordance with the specific distribution plan set forth in the resolution." Qianjinda Company argued that distribution should be made according to shareholding ratios based on the content of Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 (2014) and the resolution of the second extraordinary shareholders' meeting of Wancheng Company in 2014. In this regard, the court held that a former shareholder's right to claim profit distribution from the company should be based on whether a specific distribution plan was formed by resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders before the shareholder transferred its equity, and whether the shareholder had already acquired a specific right to claim profit distribution based on that plan. In this case, Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 (2014) of Wancheng Company and the resolution of the second extraordinary shareholders' meeting of Wancheng Company in 2014 were not specific and clear. According to Shareholders' Resolution No. 1 (2013) of Wancheng Company, the shareholders' meeting of Wancheng Company passed the profit distribution plan for 2012, which fully described the total profit available for distribution to shareholders, the profit distribution ratio, and the specific amount of profit each shareholder could receive. In contrast, in Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 (2014) of Wancheng Company, although the shareholders' meeting passed the profit distribution plan for 2013, both parties acknowledged during the court inquiry that no other profit distribution plan had been formed besides this shareholders' resolution. Moreover, the shareholders' resolution explicitly stated, "The remaining undistributed profit has not yet been paid; before June 2014, this part of the remaining undistributed profit shall be fully distributed." According to the content of this resolution, the shareholders' meeting of Wancheng Company only resolved the total amount of profit to be distributed for 2013, but did not determine a specific and clear distribution plan for the profit each shareholder should receive. The resolution of the second extraordinary shareholders' meeting of Wancheng Company in 2014 only changed the time for distribution of 2013 profit. Although Wancheng Company's articles of association provide for profit distribution according to shareholding ratios, the articles of association cannot replace a shareholders' resolution, and Qianjinda Company had no other sufficient evidence to prove that the distribution plan was specific and clear. Therefore, as a former shareholder, Qianjinda Company's right to claim profit distribution did not transform into a definite claim against the company for the profit payable to it, and the court did not support its request for Wancheng Company to pay the undistributed company profit for 2013. The first-instance judgment ordering Wancheng Company to pay Qianjinda Company the profit for 2013 and interest lacked factual and legal basis.

Regarding whether Wancheng Company should pay the undistributed company profit for 2014. In the second instance, the new evidence submitted by Qianjinda Company, including the reconciliation statement, payment voucher, and receipt notice, all indicated that the payments were for goods and could not sufficiently prove that the RMB 21 million paid by Wancheng Company was the dividend for 2014. Furthermore, the resolution of the second extraordinary shareholders' meeting of Wancheng Company in 2014 only decided on quarterly profit distribution but did not resolve the ratio or specific amount of profit to be distributed to shareholders. The audit report Lin De Hui Shen Zi [2015] No. 004 also could not represent the company's distribution plan. Therefore, the existing evidence could not prove the specific amount of profit payable by Wancheng Company to each shareholder. Qianjinda Company's appeal request that Wancheng Company pay it the undistributed profit for 2014 could not be established and should be dismissed. The first-instance court's determination in this regard was not erroneous.

Regarding whether Qianjinda Company's claim exceeded the statute of limitations. As discussed above, Qianjinda Company failed to prove that it had a specific right to claim profit distribution, so this case does not involve the issue of whether the statute of limitations has been exceeded.

In summary, Wancheng Company's appeal was established and supported. Qianjinda Company's appeal could not be established and should be dismissed. On July 8, 2019, the court rendered the civil judgment (2019) Nei Min Zhong No. 349, pursuant to Article 170(1)(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ordering: 1. Set aside the civil judgment (2018) Nei 08 Min Chu No. 60 of the Bayannaoer Intermediate People's Court of Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region; 2. Dismiss Qianjinda Company's claims. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 213,537.68, preservation fee of RMB 5,000, and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 233,715.20 shall all be borne by Qianjinda Company.

During the retrial, Qianjinda Company submitted the following new evidence: 1. Wancheng Company's profit distribution account for 2013, to prove that the distribution model for 2013 was according to equity ratio, and therefore, the distribution decision for undistributed profit for 2013 in Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 (2014) also specifically and clearly directed profit distribution according to equity ratio; 2. Wancheng Company's profit distribution account for 2014, to prove that profit was actually calculated quarterly and distributed to shareholders according to their shareholding ratios as required by the "Minutes of the Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting," and that Qianjinda Company had actually received a dividend of RMB 21 million for 2014; 3. Screenshots of emails sent by Wancheng Company's financial personnel to Qianjinda Company's financial personnel forwarding profit distribution account information, to prove that the profit distribution accounts for 2013 and 2014 came from Wancheng Company's accounting records, and that Wancheng Company was aware of its obligation to pay Qianjinda Company the claimed profit distribution.

Wancheng Company argued in its cross-examination that it agreed to the submission of the above evidence as new evidence, but that the specific data and distribution methods involved should be determined based on the original documents, which Wancheng Company held. Regarding the 2013 dividend, it revealed a pattern in Wancheng Company's profit distribution: first distributing the undistributed portion for 2012, then distributing the dividend for 2013. The distributions were not made quarterly but randomly based on cash flow.

Wancheng Company submitted the following new evidence: 1. Wancheng Gu Zi [2011] No. 1 and the profit distribution plan for 2010; 2. Wancheng Gu Zi [2012] No. 1 and the profit distribution plan for 2011, to prove that Wancheng Company's profit distribution plans over the years included the distribution ratio, the specific amount for each shareholder, and the method of distribution in cash, which were specific, clear, and executable. 3. Journal voucher and payment receipt dated January 26, 2014; 4. A copy of the accounting statement for February 2014; 5. Accounting statement for March 2014 and the enterprise income tax monthly (quarterly) prepayment return; 6. Accounting statement for June 2014; 7. Enterprise income tax monthly (quarterly) prepayment return for June 2014; 8. Journal voucher dated June 28, 2014; 9. Working capital loan contract; 10. Loan receipt from Bayannaoer Branch, Bank of China Co., Ltd.; 11. Accounting statement for July 2014; 12. Journal voucher and payment receipt dated July 14, 2014; 13. Journal voucher and payment receipt dated August 8, 2014; 14. Accounting statement for May 2015; 15. Enterprise income tax monthly (quarterly) prepayment return for June 2015, to prove Wancheng Company's financial condition. 16. Journal voucher and payment receipt dated September 9, 2014, to prove that in September 2014, the cumulative undistributed profit as of the end of August 2014 was distributed to shareholders in the amount of RMB 10 million; 17. Journal voucher and payment receipt dated January 27, 2015, to prove that in January 2015, the cumulative undistributed profit as of the end of December 2014 was distributed to shareholders in the amount of RMB 5 million.

Qianjinda Company argued in its cross-examination that the above evidence was not new evidence and should not be admitted. The authenticity of Evidence 1 and 2 is not disputed, but the purpose of proof is disputed. Wancheng Company used the fact that the board of directors prepared distribution plans for only two years to prove the process of preparing and reviewing profit distribution plans over the years, which was an overgeneralization. The authenticity and legality of Evidence 3, 12, 13, 16, and 17 are disputed. These pieces of evidence were unilaterally prepared by Wancheng Company, and their authenticity cannot be confirmed. Moreover, their content contradicts Wancheng Company's statements in the second instance. The relevance and probative value of Evidence 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 14, and 15 are disputed. These ten pieces of evidence are all accounting materials of Wancheng Company and should be based on the audit report. Insufficient internal cash flow cannot be used as a basis for failing to perform external debts. The fact that the company's internal accounting records did not record the dividends confirmed by the shareholders' resolution as due to each shareholder cannot prove that the company has no debt for profit distribution to shareholders. This court will conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the above evidence.

This court finds during the retrial that there are two issues in dispute in this retrial: first, whether Qianjinda Company has the right to require Wancheng Company to pay the unpaid profit for 2013; second, whether Qianjinda Company has the right to require Wancheng Company to distribute profit for 2014.

I. Regarding whether Qianjinda Company has the right to require Wancheng Company to pay the unpaid profit for 2013.

First, regarding the issue of whether the shareholders' resolution in question contained a specific profit distribution plan. Article 14 of Judicial Interpretation IV of the Company Law provides that "If a shareholder submits a valid resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders that contains a specific distribution plan and requests the company to distribute profits, and the company refuses to distribute profits and its defense that the resolution cannot be implemented is not established, the people's court shall order the company to distribute profits to the shareholder in accordance with the specific distribution plan set forth in the resolution." This provision requires not only that the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders passes a profit distribution resolution, but also that the content of the profit distribution plan is specific. In principle, a specific profit distribution plan should include specific distribution items such as the amount of profit to be distributed, the distribution policy, the scope of distribution, and the distribution time. The key to determining whether a profit distribution plan is specific is whether, based on the available information, the specific profit amount that the person claiming the right is entitled to receive under the plan can be determined. In this case, Shareholders' Resolution No. 2 (2014) of Wancheng Company passed the "Profit Distribution Plan for 2013" of Wancheng Company, determining the total profit to be distributed for 2013 and deciding to "complete the distribution of this remaining undistributed profit before June 2014." The subsequent "Minutes of the Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting" changed the distribution time to before the end of July 2014. The above plan indeed did not specify the distribution ratio for each shareholder or calculate the specific distribution amount for each shareholder. However, Article 10 of Wancheng Company's articles of association, concerning shareholders' rights, provides for "receiving dividends according to the capital contribution ratio," and Article 37 provides that "the profit remaining after making up losses and withdrawing statutory surplus reserve and statutory public welfare fund shall be distributed according to the shareholders' capital contribution ratio." Moreover, Wancheng Company had previously distributed profits according to capital contribution ratios. Considering the above facts comprehensively, it can be determined that the profit distribution for 2013 of Wancheng Company was made according to shareholders' shareholding ratios. In summary, the shareholders' resolution in question specified the total amount of profit distribution for 2013 and the distribution time. Together with the distribution policy in the articles of association regarding shareholders' receipt of dividends according to capital contribution ratios, the specific profit amount that Qianjinda Company should receive under the plan can be determined. Therefore, the profit distribution plan for 2013 set forth in the shareholders' resolution is specific and complies with Article 14 of Judicial Interpretation IV of the Company Law. The second-instance judgment's determination to the contrary was indeed erroneous, and this court hereby corrects it.

Second, regarding the issue of whether Qianjinda Company still retains the right to claim profit distribution after transferring its equity in Wancheng Company. In this case, Wancheng Company passed a shareholders' resolution to distribute profit for 2013 and specified a specific distribution plan. Once this resolution is made, the abstract right to claim profit distribution transforms into a specific right to claim profit distribution. The nature of the right changes from a shareholder's membership right to an ordinary creditor's right independent of shareholder rights, which does not necessarily transfer with the transfer of equity. Unless there is a clear agreement, when a shareholder transfers equity, the specific right to claim profit distribution that has already been transformed into an ordinary creditor's right does not transfer with it. Therefore, although Qianjinda Company transferred its equity in Wancheng Company to others in 2015, the parties all confirmed that the equity transfer agreement did not contain any special provisions regarding the right to claim profit distribution for 2013. Consequently, Qianjinda Company still retains the right to claim against Wancheng Company for the undistributed profit for 2013.

Third, regarding the statute of limitations. Once a profit distribution resolution specifying a concrete distribution plan is adopted, the shareholder's right to claim profit distribution is converted from an expectant right to a determinate right, and in nature, it becomes an ordinary creditor's right. When the deadline for profit distribution arrives and the company has not yet distributed the profits, the shareholder may directly request the company to pay the profits in accordance with the specific distribution plan set forth in the resolution. In this case, on March 27, 2014, Wancheng Company formed the Shareholders' Resolution Wan Cheng Gu Zi [2014] No. 2, deciding to distribute the company's undistributed profits for the year 2013 and specifying a concrete profit distribution plan. According to the Shareholders' Resolution Wan Cheng Gu Zi [2014] No. 2 and the subsequent "Minutes of the Interim Shareholders' Meeting," it was clarified that the undistributed profits for 2013 should be fully distributed by the end of July 2014. When the deadline expired and Wancheng Company still failed to distribute the profits, the right to claim profit distribution enjoyed by Qianjinda Company was infringed. Therefore, the limitation period for exercising its specific right to claim profit distribution should commence on August 1, 2014. The fact that Qianjinda Company was then a major shareholder of Wancheng Company does not affect its right to assert claims against Wancheng Company. However, Qianjinda Company only sent its first letter to Wancheng Company and its shareholders requesting payment of that portion of the profits on October 10, 2017, by which time the limitation period had already expired. Consequently, Qianjinda Company's request that Wancheng Company deliver to it the undistributed profits for 2013 cannot be supported.

In summary, the determination in the second-instance judgment regarding whether the shareholders' resolution at issue specified a concrete profit distribution plan was improper, and this court hereby corrects it. However, the conclusion that Qianjinda Company's request for Wancheng Company to pay the undistributed profits for 2013 is not supported was correct, and this court affirms it.

II. Whether Qianjinda Company has the right to demand distribution of profits for the year 2014

In this case, with respect to the undistributed profits of Wancheng Company for the year 2014 claimed by Qianjinda Company, the "Minutes of the Interim Shareholders' Meeting" only stated "2014 profits to be distributed quarterly," with no record of the amount of profits to be distributed or other matters. Although Qianjinda Company argued that the audit report recorded the profit amount for that year, an audit report cannot substitute for a shareholders' resolution. The company's decision on whether to distribute profits and how much profit to distribute should be made by a corresponding resolution. Therefore, based on the available information, the amount of profits Qianjinda Company could obtain cannot be determined, and the aforementioned shareholders' resolution does not specify a concrete profit distribution plan. Furthermore, Qianjinda Company did not submit other evidence to prove that Wancheng Company had made a concrete distribution plan for the profit distribution for 2014. Hence, Qianjinda Company's assertion that Wancheng Company should pay the undistributed profits for 2014 cannot be established. The first-instance and second-instance judgments were not improper in this regard, and this court affirms them.

In conclusion, Qianjinda Company's retrial claim cannot be established. Some of the reasoning in the second-instance judgment was improper, and this court has already corrected it. The outcome of the judgment was correct, and this court affirms it. Pursuant to Article 207, paragraph 1, and Article 170, paragraph 1, item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The civil judgment (2019) Nei Min Zhong No. 349 of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region High People's Court is affirmed.
